definitions.any_import_edge: import anywhere in the file (incl. function bodies)
definitions.module_level_edge: import executed at module import time
definitions.clean: no tree outside it imports it

cross_language.note: derived from the three graphs, not resolved a second time: shell/batch -> python by `python <file>`/`-m`/`py`, js/ts by import/require, html by <script src>. `resolved_by` names the evidence for every edge; `unresolved` and `outside_repo` account for every reference that did not become one, so the totals add up to the references looked at

javascript.note: only a specifier resolving to a file is an edge; a bare package name is a dependency and is counted separately. A relative specifier is resolved against its importer only, never tail-matched

shell.note: `python <file>`, `python -m <module>`, the `py` launcher and a `%VAR%`/`$VAR` root; a call that does not resolve is counted by reason. Unlike js/html a shell path may be tail-matched, because the launcher layer was written for a flat layout, and only a UNIQUE match counts

html.note: <script src> only; inline <script> bodies are not parsed. A relative src is resolved against the template only, never tail-matched

rust.note: `mod name;` and `use crate::a::b` resolved to a file; an external crate is a dependency and is counted separately. Module paths are exact, so nothing is tail-matched

python_graph.note: file -> file, resolved against the src-relative package path that the tree-level graph already assumes; `from X import y` is followed to X/y.py, and a name that is not a module is counted separately rather than called a broken import

liftability.note: a shard is liftable when no file outside it references a file inside it, in ANY instrumented language -- a .bat driver that calls into a python shard blocks it just as an importer does. Each blocker names its graph so the two remedies stay distinct

files.note: every file under every root lands in exactly one bucket; `code` is the population the per-language graphs and the shard plan address, `generated` is tool output counted but not authored, and `unclassified` must be empty -- a non-empty list is a hole in this table, not a category

languages.note: a language is instrumented iff a graph covers it (GRAPH_LANGUAGES); `uninstrumented` names what is COUNTED but not resolved, and is empty when every code file in src/ lands in a graph. Inline <script> bodies are not parsed, and a bare js/ts/html specifier is a package dependency, never an edge

limits: static scan: importlib/__import__ and string-based plugin loading (the worm registry) are invisible, so runtime coupling is higher
cycle detection reports direct mutual pairs per language; the transitive closure in `contracts.cycles_transitive` is tree-level only
dependencies are package-level for js/ts and html: a bare specifier is counted as a package dependency, never an edge
